title: Protein Extraction from Mammalian Cells (RIPA Lysis)
purpose: To prepare whole-cell protein lysates from adherent or suspension mammalian cells for Western blotting, immunoprecipitation and immunoassays.
principle: RIPA buffer combines NP-40, sodium deoxycholate and a little SDS to solubilise membrane, cytoplasmic and nuclear proteins [1][3]. Protease and phosphatase inhibitors preserve proteins and phosphorylation, and everything is kept cold [1][2]. Centrifugation removes debris and a BCA assay sets equal loading [1][3].

materials.detail: 50 mM Tris pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 5 mM EDTA, 1% NP-40, 0.5% deoxycholate, 0.1% SDS; 4 °C up to 1 month [1]
50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.6, 150 mM NaCl, 1% NP-40, 0.5% deoxycholate, 0.1% SDS [3]
PMSF and sodium orthovanadate, as used in one lab protocol [4]

steps.text: Chill PBS, tubes and the centrifuge to 4 °C. Add inhibitor cocktail to RIPA immediately before use and keep it on ice [1][2].
Grow cells to about 80% confluence (adherent) or 1–2 × 10⁶ cells/mL (suspension) [1][2].
Adherent: place the dish on ice, aspirate medium and wash once or twice with 10 mL ice-cold PBS [1][4].
Add RIPA directly: about 200–500 µL for a 100 mm dish, 250–500 µL for 60 mm, 200–400 µL per 6-well well. Optimise per cell type [1][3].
Scrape the cells, pipette the lysate about 20 times and transfer to a pre-chilled tube [1][4].
Suspension: pellet at 300 × g for 5 min, wash once with 5–10 mL ice-cold PBS and spin again [1][2].
Resuspend suspension cells in 10–100 µL RIPA per 10⁶ cells [1][2].
Incubate on ice with occasional mixing [1][3].
If viscous from genomic DNA, sonicate (three 2 s pulses, low-moderate power, 1 min on ice between) and incubate 15 min more [1][2][3].
Centrifuge at 13,000–14,000 × g at 4 °C and transfer the supernatant to fresh pre-chilled tubes, leaving the pellet [1][3][4].
Measure protein by BCA; one RIPA vendor advises against Bradford with RIPA detergents [1][3].
Aim for 1–5 mg/mL for Western blotting [2].
Aliquot and store at −20 °C (−80 °C long term); avoid freeze–thaw. Add Laemmli buffer and heat when ready to run gels [1][2].

results: Clear supernatant with protein at roughly 1–5 mg/mL (adjust volume to cell number) [2].
Strong, even bands for abundant proteins and preserved phospho-signal when phosphatase inhibitors are used.
controls: Probe a loading control (e.g. actin or tubulin) on the Western blot
Make BCA standards in the same RIPA diluent
Keep a no-inhibitor aliquot only if testing degradation

troubleshooting.fix: Sonicate briefly or pass through a needle, then re-spin [1][3]

troubleshooting.cause: Too much RIPA for the cell number
troubleshooting.fix: Reduce volume or pool plates; re-quantify [1]

troubleshooting.problem: Lost enzyme activity or binding partners
troubleshooting.fix: Use a milder buffer for kinase or co-IP work [3]
Use BCA with standards in RIPA [3]

safety: RIPA contains SDS and NP-40 (irritants); PMSF and sodium orthovanadate are toxic: use gloves, and a fume hood where indicated [4].
Treat lysates from human or primate cells as potentially infectious at the biosafety level your institution requires.
Dispose of inhibitor-containing waste as chemical waste.
